title: Our Lady, Help of Christians (Don Bosco Devotion)
summary: Not a Marian apparition in the formal sense, but a centuries-old title honoring Mary's intercession for the Church, given lasting devotional force by a feast instituted by Pope Pius VII in 1815 and popularized worldwide through St. John Bosco.

blocks.text: 1. A Title and a Feast, Not a Formal Apparition

Unlike Lourdes or Fátima, this devotion does not rest on a single dated apparition to a named visionary that the Church formally investigated and approved. It is a title of Mary—'Help of Christians'—that grew out of the Church's historical experience of her intercession.

blocks.title: A Category Distinction
blocks.text: This devotion belongs to a different category of Marian piety than an approved apparition. It expresses a ongoing conviction of faith rather than a single private revelation event.

The invocation 'Help of Christians' (Auxilium Christianorum) traces to the 16th century, gaining special prominence after the Battle of Lepanto in 1571. Over time, it became a title expressing Mary's continuous defense and aid for the Church in times of trial.

St. John Bosco (1815–1888) became the title's greatest champion, placing his entire apostolate for youth under Mary's guidance. In 1865, he began building the Basilica of Mary Help of Christians in Turin, relying entirely on divine providence for funding.

blocks.title: The Conviction of St. John Bosco
blocks.text: “Trust in Mary Help of Christians and you will see what miracles are. Have faith in her and she will cover you with her mantle of protection.”

Bosco also founded the Salesians and, alongside St. Maria Domenica Mazzarello, the Daughters of Mary Help of Christians. Traditional accounts of his prophetic dreams regarding the site of the Turin Basilica are treated by the Church as private spiritual experiences rather than binding revelations.
For he has regarded the low estate of his handmaiden; for behold, henceforth all generations will call me blessed.
Exegesis: The title expresses the Church's ongoing faith that Mary's spiritual motherhood continues from heaven, interceding for the pilgrim Church without introducing new doctrines.

Pope Pius VII instituted the liturgical feast of Our Lady, Help of Christians on September 15, 1815 (assigned to May 24), in thanksgiving for his return to Rome following years of imprisonment under Napoleon.

blocks.title: CCC 67 / Church Approval Status
blocks.text: There is no formal apparition to investigate here. Per CCC 67, papal approval of this feast and its associated devotions honors Mary's providential help and invites authentic piety, without adding new articles to the deposit of faith.
Devotion to Our Lady, Help of Christians encourages active trust in God's care during personal and ecclesial struggles, inspiring practical works of education, charity, and youth ministry.

blocks.title: Central Lesson
blocks.text: Our Lady, Help of Christians points to Mary as a constant spiritual mother and protector, urging the faithful to translate trust in her intercession into generous service toward others.

blocks.title: Traditional Salesian Invocation
blocks.text: Mary, Help of Christians, pray for us. St. John Bosco, pray for us. Amen.
